chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abd Allah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'So mention the Name of Allah upon them, standing in a row.' He said: 'That is when they are lined up for slaughter. You tie their forelegs from the hooves to the knees, and the falling of their sides is when they fall upon the ground.'
ai.seo_question: When exactly should the Name of Allah be mentioned during animal sacrifice according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the precise timing and physical preparation for the ritual slaughter (dhabh) of animals, linking the Quranic command to invoke Allah's name with the moment the animal is lined up (sawaff) for sacrifice. It highlights the scholarly emphasis on the continuity of the ritual act, specifying that the invocation begins when the animal is secured—tying the forelegs from the hoof to the knee—and concludes as it falls, ensuring the sanctity of the meat through proper adherence to Sunnah.

en.hubeali: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Abdullah Bin Sinan,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws regarding the Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic [22:36] therefore Mention the Name of Allah on these as they stand in a row. Heasws said: ‘That is where they are stood in a row for the sacrifice. You would tie down its hand in what is between the hooves up to the knees, and [22:36] then when they fall down - is when they fall upon the ground’.
en.sarwar: 1. Abu Ali al-Ash’ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan ibn Yahya from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sinan who has said the following: “

This is about the words of Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, ’Pronounce the name of Allah on them while lined up. . . [22:36] He (the Imam) said that this is when they are lined up for slaughtering. When their front legs are tied down between the feet to the knees, and ’falling of their sides’ is a reference to their reaching the ground.’”
